item.text:
I refactored the code around two concrete improvements.

[InsertionSort.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/035_insertion_sort/InsertionSort.java:5) now carries subrange state through a private `Range` type instead of threading raw `fromIndex`/`toIndex` pairs through every helper. That removes a fair amount of index-handling duplication and makes the whole-array and partial-array paths share the same internal flow. I also made the API symmetric by adding range-based `sortedCopy(...)` overloads for both `int[]` and generic arrays, so partial sorting no longer requires mutation.

I updated [InsertionSortDemo.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/035_insertion_sort/InsertionSortDemo.java:8) to show the new partial-copy behavior, and expanded [InsertionSortSelfTest.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/035_insertion_sort/InsertionSortSelfTest.java:8) with coverage for primitive and generic range-copy paths.

Verification passed with `javac InsertionSort.java InsertionSortDemo.java InsertionSortSelfTest.java`, `java InsertionSortDemo`, and `java InsertionSortSelfTest`.
